title: Scheme tests of coproducts of fppf sheaves give clopen partitions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], fix a big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $I$ be a small set in that convention. Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be sheaves of sets on this site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Their coproduct $C=\coprod_{i\in I}G_i$ in sheaves (the colimit of the discrete $I$-indexed diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) exists; its coprojections $c_i:G_i\to C$ are monomorphisms (injective on sections). For every site object $T$ and every section $a\in C(T)$, there is a unique partition $T=\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and unique sections $a_i\in G_i(T_i)$ such that $c_i(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$. Empty pieces are allowed. If $h_T(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,T)$, the square determined by $T_i\to T$, $a_i:h_{T_i}\to G_i$, $a:h_T\to C$, and $c_i$ is cartesian: $h_{T_i}\simeq h_T\times_CG_i$. For every morphism $b:Z\to T$ of site objects, the partition and sections for $a|_Z$ are $b^{-1}(T_i)$ and the restrictions of $a_i$; conversely any such clopen partition with sections in the $G_i$ glues to a unique section of $C(T)$. For $I=\varnothing$, $C(T)$ is a singleton when $T$ is empty and is empty otherwise.

source.place: Tag 0F15 (lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed) and Tag 02WO (lemma-representable-sheaf-coproduct-sheaves), applied to each summand versus the coproduct of the others; the set-indexed form uses the construction of a coproduct as sheafification in sites.tex Tag 00WI (lemma-colimit-sheaves).

proof.text: Work in the small universe-sized model of the site specified in [def-weil-size-convention]. Define the presheaf $P$ by $P(V)=\coprod_{i\in I}G_i(V)$, with restrictions preserving the label $i$. By [lem-trf-sieve-set-sheafification-exists], its sheafification $C=P^\#$ exists. For any sheaf $H$, a natural map $P\to H$ is exactly a family of natural maps $G_i\to H$, by evaluating on the labelled pairs $(i,s)$. The sheafification adjunction therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C,H)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(G_i,H)$. This is precisely the coproduct universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with $c_i(s)=\eta(i,s)$. This argument works also for empty $I$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], every $a\in C(T)$ is represented on an fppf covering $\{g_\alpha:U_\alpha\to T\}$ by labelled sections $(i_\alpha,s_\alpha)$ of $P$. Also, if $c_i(s)=c_j(t)$ on a scheme $V$, that lemma gives an fppf covering on which $(i,s)$ and $(j,t)$ are equal in $P$. If $i=j$, the sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] implies $s=t$. Hence every $c_i$ is injective on every section set; componentwise cancellation also proves it is monic. If $i\ne j$, no member of this further covering can exist, since equality of labelled pairs would imply $i=j$. Thus it is the empty covering; joint surjectivity [def-pc-fppf-site] forces $V$ empty. Every sheaf has one section over the empty scheme, by its empty covering and the same equalizer condition.

source.place: Tag 0F15 (lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed), local representatives and empty mixed intersections; sites.tex Tag 00WK

proof.text: The images $g_\alpha(U_\alpha)$ are open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], since covering morphisms are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-fppf-site]. When $i_\alpha\ne i_\beta$, the restrictions of $a$ to $U_\alpha\times_TU_\beta$ are simultaneously in the two different summands, so Step 2 makes this fibre product empty. Their images in $T$ are disjoint: indeed let $W=g_\alpha(U_\alpha)$ with its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. The factorization $U_\alpha\to W$ is surjective. Its base change along $U_\beta\times_TW\to W$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], while its source is $U_\alpha\times_TU_\beta$ (the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]). It follows that $U_\beta\times_TW$ is empty. This scheme is the inverse image open of $W$ in $U_\beta$, proving the claimed disjointness.

source.place: Tag 0F15, disjoint open images; morphisms.tex Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open) and Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective)

proof.text: For each $i$ put $T_i=\bigcup_{\alpha:i_\alpha=i}g_\alpha(U_\alpha)$, with its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Step 3 shows these opens are pairwise disjoint, and joint surjectivity of the covering [def-pc-fppf-site] shows that they cover $T$. Each $T_i$ is also closed because its complement is the union of all the other $T_j$. This is a scheme coproduct decomposition: a family of maps $T_i\to Y$ glues uniquely to $T\to Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], since all mixed intersections are empty. Thus the disjoint open inclusions have the required coproduct universal property, with arbitrary empty pieces allowed.

source.place: Tag 0F15, the decomposition into disjoint opens; Tag 02WO (lemma-representable-sheaf-coproduct-sheaves), the resulting scheme decomposition

proof.text: Base change the covering $\{U_\alpha\to T\}$ to $T_i$. By the site axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], this is an fppf covering. Its members with label $i$ are $U_\alpha$ and its other members are empty, by Step 3. On two members with label $i$, the sections $s_\alpha,s_\beta$ have equal images under $c_i$, since both images restrict $a$; their restrictions agree by the injectivity proved in Step 2. Supply the unique $G_i$ section on every empty member. The sheaf equalizer condition therefore glues these sections uniquely to $a_i\in G_i(T_i)$. The same condition for $C$ gives $c_i(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$, since this equality holds on the pulled-back covering.

source.place: Tag 0F15, the verification omitted after the clopen decomposition: glue the local sections using the sheaf condition

proof.text: Suppose $T=\coprod_iV_i$ is another clopen partition and $b_i\in G_i(V_i)$ satisfies $c_i(b_i)=a|_{V_i}$. On $T_i\cap V_j$, these equalities identify sections coming from labels $i$ and $j$. For $i\ne j$ Step 2 forces this open scheme to be empty. Since the $V_j$ cover $T$, this gives $T_i\subseteq V_i$; reversing the two partitions gives $V_i\subseteq T_i$. The open subschemes coincide, and then $a_i=b_i$ by the injectivity of $c_i$. Thus the partition and its sections are unique, independently of all choices of local representatives.

source.place: Tag 0F15, uniqueness in the omitted fibre-product verification

proof.text: Fix $i$ and a test scheme $Z$. A section of $h_T\times_CG_i$ on $Z$ is a pair $(b,s)$ with $b:Z\to T$, $s\in G_i(Z)$ and $c_i(s)=b^*a$; this is the sectionwise fibre-product equation. On the inverse image open $Z_j=b^{-1}(T_j)$, it identifies $c_i(s|_{Z_j})$ with $c_j(b^*a_j)$. Step 2 makes $Z_j$ empty for $j\ne i$. The $Z_j$ cover $Z$, so $b^{-1}(T_i)=Z$, and $b$ factors uniquely through the open subscheme $T_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion]: its underlying map has image in that open and its structure-sheaf map restricts there. Injectivity of $c_i$ then forces $s$ to be the pullback of $a_i$. Conversely every $Z\to T_i$ gives such a pair. These assignments are inverse and commute with precomposition in $Z$, since both use only composition and restriction of sections. They give the natural identification $h_{T_i}\simeq h_T\times_CG_i$, and hence the asserted cartesian square. Here a section $a$ gives the natural transformation $h_T\to C$ explicitly by $b\mapsto b^*a$, so no additional identification theorem is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F15, complete verification of the omitted assertion that the open represents the summand pullback

proof.text: For $b:Z\to T$, inverse images of the $T_i$ form a disjoint clopen cover of $Z$, and the restrictions of the $a_i$ satisfy the equations for $b^*a$ by naturality of $c_i$. Step 6 identifies them with its unique partition and component sections. Conversely, for any disjoint clopen partition and sections in its summands, apply $c_i$ to the sections. They agree on mixed intersections because those are empty and $C(\varnothing)$ is a singleton (Step 2). These sections glue uniquely to a section of $C(T)$ by the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Open coverings are fppf coverings [def-pc-fppf-site]; Step 6 recovers exactly the prescribed partition and sections.

source.place: Tag 0F15, restriction and sheaf gluing of the clopen pieces

proof.text: Finally let $I=\varnothing$. Then $P(V)=\varnothing$ for every $V$. If $a\in P^\#(T)$ existed, its local representatives supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] would require a section of $P$ on every covering member. Thus the covering has no members, and joint surjectivity [def-pc-fppf-site] forces $T=\varnothing$. When $T=\varnothing$, the empty covering and the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] give exactly one section of $C$. This proves the stated empty-index formula and also accounts for the empty partition in every earlier clause.

lean.statement: theorem fppfSheaf_coproduct_partition {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type (max u v)} (G : I → Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) : (∃ (C : Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) (c : ∀ i, G i ⟶ C), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk C c))) ∧ (∀ (C : Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) (c : ∀ i, G i ⟶ C), IsColimit (Cofan.mk C c) → (∀ i, Mono (c i) ∧ ∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective ((c i).hom.app (op T))) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : C.obj.obj (op T)), ∃! d : FppfCoproductPartition G T, d.MapsTo c a) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : C.obj.obj (op T)) (d : FppfCoproductPartition G T), d.MapsTo c a → (Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk T.left (fun i ↦ (d.opens i).ι)))) ∧ (∀ i, IsPullback (uliftYoneda.{v}.map (fppfPartitionInclusion T (d.opens i))) (uliftYonedaEquiv.{v}.symm (d.sections i)) (uliftYonedaEquiv.{v}.symm a) (c i).hom) ∧ (∀ (Z : Over S) (b : Z ⟶ T), ∃ e : FppfCoproductPartition G Z, e.MapsTo c (C.obj.map b.op a) ∧ ∀ i, e.opens i = b.left ⁻¹ᵁ d.opens i ∧ HEq (e.sections i) ((G i).obj.map (fppfPartitionRestriction b (d.opens i)).op (d.sections i)))) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (d : FppfCoproductPartition G T), ∃! a : C.obj.obj (op T), d.MapsTo c a) ∧ (IsEmpty I → ∀ T : Over S, (IsEmpty T.left → Nonempty (Unique (C.obj.obj (op T)))) ∧ (Nonempty T.left → IsEmpty (C.obj.obj (op T)))))
lean.note: The auxiliary record packages exactly the clopen pieces and their sections; MapsTo is their component equation. Coproduct existence is existential, and all further assertions apply to every colimit cofan, without assuming a global sheafification instance on the big site. The summand squares are expressed in presheaves, equivalently in sheaves, since representables are fppf sheaves and sheaf inclusion creates limits. ULift only places representables in the common coefficient universe.
